# Resolving a conflicted document: both sides moved, so merge combines them
# against the copy from the last sync. Edits in different places merge
# cleanly and publishing is truthful afterwards; edits to the same line get
# conflict markers, and publishing refuses until they are gone.

fulcrum sync

# We append a paragraph; the server rewrites the opening line.
cp local-append.md skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md
srv edit skill-corpus-writing-specs 'Name the behavior, not the implementation.' 'Name the behavior. Server said so.'
fulcrum -code 1 status
grep 'CONFLICTED' last-stdout.txt

fulcrum merge
grep 'merged skill-corpus-writing-specs.md cleanly' last-stdout.txt

# Both edits survive, and the doc is merely drifted against current now.
grep 'Ours, appended at the end.' skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md
grep 'Name the behavior. Server said so.' skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md
fulcrum -code 1 status
grep 'drifted' last-stdout.txt
! grep 'CONFLICTED' last-stdout.txt

# Publishing after a merge is based on the CURRENT version, not flagged stale.
fulcrum publish --yes --note merged-cleanly
grep 'Proposal #101 submitted' last-stdout.txt
! grep 'flagged stale' last-stdout.txt

# Now both sides rewrite the same line.
fulcrum sync --force
cp same-line.md skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md
srv edit skill-corpus-writing-specs 'Name the behavior. Server said so.' 'Name the behavior. Server again.'

fulcrum -code 1 merge
grep 'conflict' last-stdout.txt
grep '<<<<<<< your local edits' skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md
grep '>>>>>>> the current version in Fulcrum' skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md
# Both sides are preserved for the human to choose between.
grep 'My words instead.' skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md
grep 'Server again.' skills/skill-corpus-writing-specs.md

# Publishing refuses to submit markers — no second proposal is created.
fulcrum publish --yes --note still-conflicted
grep 'unresolved conflict markers' last-stdout.txt
srv count 1

-- local-append.md --
---
name: corpus-writing-specs
description: How this team writes request specs.
---

# corpus-writing-specs

Name the behavior, not the implementation. One expectation of intent
per example; shared setup in let blocks.

Ours, appended at the end.
-- same-line.md --
---
name: corpus-writing-specs
description: How this team writes request specs.
---

# corpus-writing-specs

Name the behavior. My words instead. One expectation of intent
per example; shared setup in let blocks.
